$comment: Single source of truth for imagery. `npm run manifest` regenerates prompts/image-manifest.md from this file. Drop a real file into public/images/<kind>/<filename> and the placeholder plate is replaced automatically at build time.

images.subject: A second-floor apartment window at dusk, one of many, the only one lit; the glass carries a faint reflection of the street trees behind the viewer.
images.concept: Two worlds occupying the same surface. You can attend to the room or to the reflection, never both at once.
images.purpose: Sets the essay's premise before a word of it is read.

images.subject: A field-guide plate of a single room, drawn twice: once complete in fine hairline ink, once as the four or five marks that survived being looked at.
images.concept: The paraphrase. What the editor kept.
images.purpose: Gives the pull quote something to argue with rather than decorate.

images.subject: An old dog lying at the edge of a rectangle of afternoon light on a wood floor, having moved with it; the previous position still visible as a dent in a rug.
images.concept: Sustained attention without effort. The animal is better at this than you are.
images.purpose: Carries the essay's central practical claim: noticing is a matter of speed, not will.

images.subject: An enormous flat bank of weather over a grey lake, with one very small figure standing on a breakwater far right of centre.
images.concept: Scale as an attention device. The eye has to travel to find the person.
images.purpose: The book's first long exhale. No text, no folio.
images.revision: Keep the horizon clear of the fold; the figure must sit fully on the recto.

images.subject: Wet sidewalk after rain, a scatter of starlings on a wire above it, arranged by accident into something that reads like handwriting.
images.concept: The world composing itself without intending to.
images.purpose: Opens Part I on an image of a pattern that was always there.

images.subject: Four strangers at a crosswalk, all looking at four different things, their shadows overlapping into a single shape.
images.concept: Four separate paraphrases of one street corner.
images.purpose: Interrupts the text at the foot of the verso, so the spread has weight where it would otherwise trail off.

images.essay: Why Ordinary Days May Be the Point of Life
images.spread: Essay opener · over (crossover, two pages, title reversed out)
images.subject: An empty domestic kitchen at six o'clock in October, low orange light coming in flat across the counter and one chair. Nobody in the room. A pan on the stove, a cloth over the tap, the day clearly still in progress.
images.concept: The room the essay remembers. Warm, unremarkable, and completely specific.
images.purpose: Sets the emotional temperature of the whole book before the first sentence.
images.revision: Title reverses out of this image — keep the right two-fifths quiet and mid-dark so 96 pt type stays legible. Nothing important on the fold.

images.essay: Why Ordinary Days May Be the Point of Life
images.subject: Two pairs of shoes left by a back door, one knocked over, on a worn mat. Morning light, low angle, floor filling most of the frame.
images.concept: The first ordinary evidence of a day nobody photographed.

images.essay: Why Ordinary Days May Be the Point of Life
images.subject: Steam rising off a kettle or a mug against a bright window, mostly backlit, the object nearly a silhouette.
images.concept: Something happening that is over in four seconds and repeats ten thousand times.
images.purpose: The smallest note in the sequence.

images.essay: Why Ordinary Days May Be the Point of Life
images.subject: A dog asleep on a floor in the middle of a room, seen from across the room so the dog is small and the empty floor is the subject.
images.concept: The animal that does not distinguish a Tuesday from a birthday.
images.purpose: The widest, calmest beat in the sequence.

images.essay: Why Ordinary Days May Be the Point of Life
images.subject: A rectangle of late October light lying across a wall and part of a doorframe. No objects, no people. The light is the subject and it is obviously moving.
images.concept: The ninety seconds the essay is actually about.
images.purpose: The image the closing spread pays off.
images.revision: This one carries the essay. If only one image in the sequence is right, make it this one.

images.essay: Why Ordinary Days May Be the Point of Life
images.subject: A window at dusk from inside, the glass beginning to act as a mirror, a suburban street barely visible beyond it.
images.purpose: Ends the sequence on an exhale.

images.essay: Why Ordinary Days May Be the Point of Life
images.subject: A field-guide plate of a photograph album drawn open, its pages catalogued like specimens: six mounted rectangles with tiny handwritten-looking tick labels beneath, and a great deal of empty cream paper around them where the unphotographed days would be.
images.concept: The album as a very small sample of a very large life.
images.purpose: Gives the pull quote its counter-argument in the same spread.
images.revision: No legible text anywhere. The tick labels must read as marks, not words.

images.essay: Why Ordinary Days May Be the Point of Life
images.spread: Image + essay · band (crossover, top of both pages)
images.subject: A kitchen table after a meal, seen straight on from standing height: plates not yet cleared, one chair pushed back, an ordinary amount of mess. Late evening interior light.
images.concept: The life the trip is an interruption in.
images.revision: Crossover — keep the pushed-back chair fully on the verso and nothing of interest within 15 mm of the fold.
